items.title: An operation per editor verb, with the UI and the agent both dispatching it

must_fix.evidence: The registry has one operation (map_set_settings) and 128 actions are on the unmigrated allowlist. The brief asks for one workflow first, with the allowlist shrinking.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/tests/operations_have_two_front_ends.rs::the_allowlist_of_unmigrated_actions_only_shrinks

items.title: The kit's library and policy are re-read by a full project reload, which is slow and loses the open map

must_fix.evidence: watch.rs::adopt re-opens the whole project for a library change, because only Project::open knows how to merge every bound kit. A per-kit re-read would be better.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/src/watch.rs::adopt

items.title: The operation log has a single-writer assumption, so two agents would claim the same sequence number

must_fix.evidence: ops.rs::next_seq counts the lines in the log, and the MCP server and the editor are separate processes that could both append. An advisory file lock would fix it.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/src/ops.rs::next_seq

items.title: Enclosure wish and weight are hard-coded in the editor, so an author who wants more enclosed rooms edits Rust

must_fix.evidence: editor.rs ENCLOSURE_WISH = 0.25 and ENCLOSURE_WEIGHT = 200 are not in rules.ron, so they are not authored and cannot be tuned without a rebuild.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/src/editor.rs (ENCLOSURE_WISH, ENCLOSURE_WEIGHT)

items.title: No crate in this workspace is published to crates.io, so the first publication is undecided

must_fix.evidence: cargo info for all seven crates says 'could not find ... in registry'. There is no published baseline, so no release can be made and no pre-publish gate has a version to check against.

items.evidence: cargo info bevy_emerge_core@0.1.0 (and the other six)

items.title: The chooser's new-map dialog writes name, bounds, origin and note directly, outside the registry

must_fix.evidence: chooser.rs:5907-5910 (write_settings) and chooser.rs:662 (write_bash) write the map's settings without dispatching map_set_settings. They are a different subject -- a new map with no open map -- and the honest claim is that one operation has two front ends, not that every verb does.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/src/chooser.rs::write_settings

items.title: Frame time is unmeasurable through MCP and unreliable on a shared machine
items.evidence: emerge_state has no frame clock; bevy_debugger/status tick counting gave 33.1 / 20.2 / 67.2 ms medians at load 2 agents / idle / load-avg 30.8. A per-frame CPU-time diagnostic in emerge_state would separate the editor from the machine.

items.title: Signature-reading ratchets cannot see resources inside #[derive(SystemParam)] bundles
items.evidence: B-005 introduced 32 bundles; the_sweep_is_finished and every_resource_says_what_a_door_does_to_it read fn signatures, so a bare Res in a bundle used by an on_* observer would pass. on_shelf_click was kept unbundled for this reason; the ratchets should resolve bundle fields.

items.title: The person's Cmd+Z cannot reject an agent's change; only emerge_undo_operation can
items.evidence: Agent applies go to the log but not to EditorState's stack. User problem: the developer sees an agent's change and wants it gone; frequency: every agent proposal they dislike; saving: one keystroke instead of asking the agent; risk: ordering the agent's lines against the person's stack, and a second front end for the same undo.

items.title: The receipt sits in UNDER's value column, so it reads as the value of UNDER

must_fix.evidence: docs/loop/iterations/assets/2026-10-21-15be05c/window-after.png: 'size back: map is 300 x 26 x 1120 m...' directly under the empty UNDER label

items.evidence: Not must-fix (one yes: the text says what it is). A label or its own block would end the ambiguity.

items.title: The hint row (Field::Hint) is zero tall when empty, so a hint pushes EDGES, MAP SIZE and the lists down

must_fix.evidence: editor.rs ghost: state.hint set while a surface/mounted piece is armed over floor it cannot stand on, cleared where it fits; same shape as B-009 (reviewer, 2026-10-21)

items.evidence: Not must-fix (needs a surface or mounted piece armed). Fold into one reserved status slot with the receipt rather than reserving a second blank row.

items.title: Snip: the developer drags a rectangle over the editor and the agent receives the crop plus where they were
items.evidence: Asked for by the developer 2026-10-21. User problem: pointing at a visual problem means describing it in words; frequency: every visual review; saving: the agent gets the crop, map, camera, panel text and placements under the rectangle in one call; risk: a new gesture and a text field (register in editor::Fields), and snips are files in the project (confine and name them). Progress 2026-10-21 (556801e): the agent half shipped as emerge_snip { label, rect } (crop of a window-pixel rectangle, with path and state). Still open: the human drag gesture in the editor (UI state machine plus a registered operation that emits the snip).

items.title: An action search palette over keys::Action::ALL (renzora's command palette)
items.evidence: From the renzora/engine survey (crates/renzora_command_palette/src/modal.rs). User problem: an action is reachable only by knowing its chord; frequency: high (128+ actions); saving: two keystrokes instead of a chord hunt; risk: the palette must refuse what the current keys::Context refuses, through Status::problem.

items.title: In a narrow window (about 900 logical px) the viewport is a sliver between the two fixed-width panels

must_fix.evidence: docs/loop/iterations/assets/2026-10-21-63e6631/window-narrow.png: about 70 logical px of viewport at 1800 x 1406 physical

items.evidence: Not must-fix: ordinary windows are wider, and widening the window is the workaround. Panels that shrink, or one that folds away, would fix it.

items.title: The full undo history as a list, with click-to-jump (the rest of renzora's history panel)
items.evidence: E-016 shipped the next undo and redo, named. User problem: going back several steps is blind repetition; frequency: occasional; saving: one click instead of N Cmd+Z; risk: a jump of N steps is N guarded undos, each of which can refuse.

items.title: Sanctuary lifts its roads in code (town.rs:60 ROAD_LIFT = 0.15), so the editor cannot know the game's draw order from data
items.evidence: Content hard-coded in the consumer. The editor now draws roads over fields by its own rule (smaller footprint on top), which matches for this map. Authoring the order as Placed::paint in the map would make game and editor agree by data. Consumer change: tell Sanctuary's agents via AGENTS_CHAT.md (append only).

items.title: Ghosts and previews do not get draw levels, and relevel is O(n^2) per map change
items.evidence: From the z-fight fix (bd5116a/63e6631): ghost/preview spawns in editor.rs and redraw_stamps get no paint or lift, so a ghost over a field can draw differently from the committed piece; relevel_placements compares every pair when the map changes (727 pieces: about 0.5 M pairs).

items.title: A frame key for the person (Home: the locked placement, or the whole map)
items.evidence: Built in the 2026-10-21 frame iteration and taken out: a new keys::Action that is not a registry operation grows the unmigrated allowlist, which operations_have_two_front_ends pins at 128 and says must be paid for by migrating one in the same commit. Ship it together with one migration. The framing itself (view::frame_box, editor::resolve_frame/apply_frame) is ready; the person's wheel can now zoom out to the whole map.

items.title: Possible +1.5 ms frame time between b6ee5af and 8c97677 (not significant: paired t = 1.79, n = 9)
items.evidence: target/loop/2026-10-21-b6ee5af/ab*.txt; the commit adds no per-frame work beyond view::drive reading the viewport aspect. Check with a profiler (Tracy or bevy_debugger frame timings) before claiming either way.

items.title: A map whose stacking does not resolve opens unframed on the 18 m close-up

must_fix.evidence: reviewer P3 of the E-022 iteration (docs/loop/iterations/2026-10-21-view-b51da72.md): the open-framed path resolves the whole map through resolve_frame, which needs stack heights; when stacking fails it shows the stacking toast and leaves the old close-up

items.evidence: Not must-fix: only maps with an unresolvable stack, and the toast already says why; emerge_frame_view {target: map} or the wheel still frames it. The whole-map box needs no stack heights (editor::map_bounds), so framing could fall back to it.
